text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended weaker but off the day's lows in trading dominated by pre-expiry dealings and the nearby March/May spread. March lost $1.10 to close at $303.60 per tonne, while May gave up $1.30 to close at $300.60 per tonne. There was no fresh news to give the market direction. In New York raw sugar futures closed lower across the board on speculative selling centered around the March/May spread. March lost 9 points to close at 10.51 cents/lb, while May ended 3 points lower at 10.53 cents/lb. The outer months lost between 3 and 4 points.

INDIA - Indian sugar production in December 1996 reached 2.413 million tonnes, raw value, down from 2.590 million tonnes produced the same month the previous year. That brought total production since the beginning of the campaign (October) up to 3.891 million tonnes, 4.4 percent less than was produced the same period in 1995. Total production in crop year 1995/96 reached a record of 17.9 million tonnes, up from 15.9 million tonnes the previous year. Production in 1996/97 is expected to be lower due to adverse weather and overproduction in the past two years. However, the decline will not affect the country's trading position as stocks are still excessive.

NEW ZEALAND - Sugar imports in December 1996 amounted to 26,331 tonnes, raw value, which brought total imports in calendar year 1996 up to a record high of 263,774 tonnes compared to 210,379 tonnes in 1995 and 215,117 tonnes in 1994. The major country of origin in calendar year 1996 was Australia with 170,599 tonnes raws against 175,261 tonnes and 84,899 tonnes whites compared to 30,953 tonnes. Sugar exports in December 1996 amounted to 2,752 tonnes, which brought total exports in calendar year 1996 up 21,407 tonnes compared to 20,270 tonnes in 1995 and 16,007 tonnes in 1994. Major countries of destination in 1996 were French Polynesia with 6,056 tonnes whites against 5,175 tonnes and New Caledonia with 5,180 tonnes compared to 4,626 tonnes. ITALY - Sugar imports in September 1996 amounted to 22,614 tonnes, raw value, up from 17,353 tonnes imported in the like period the previous year.
